takeaway: In adults the femoral head is supplied mainly by the medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries via retinacular vessels; the ligamentum teres artery matters in childhood.

question.text: Concerning the blood supply to the femoral head, which of the following statements is correct?

answer.text: Lateral and medial circumflex femoral arteries supply the femoral head via retinacula.

lines.text: In children, the artery of the ligamentum teres matters more.
In adults, this obturator branch gives only a negligible supply.
The main supply comes from the medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries.
Their branches run back under the hip capsule in longitudinal bands, the retinacula, to reach the head.
Vessels from the diaphysis add only a small supply in adults.
That is why an intracapsular fracture, tearing these retinacular vessels, risks avascular necrosis,
while extracapsular fractures leave them intact.
lines.say: (sigh) while extracapsular fractures leave them intact.

lines.text: So the answer: the circumflex arteries, via the retinacula.
